accepted.s: Shivaji was crowned at which place and in which year?
accepted.x: Shivaji's coronation took place at Raigad in 1674.
accepted.tq: Use the direct place-year pair and distinguish it from other important Maratha forts.
accepted.sec: ■ Coronation - place, year, title  [other exams]

accepted.s: On which date did Shivaji's coronation take place at Raigad?
accepted.x: Shivaji was crowned at Raigad on 6 June 1674.
accepted.tq: Separate the precise date from the broader coronation year.
accepted.sec: ■ Coronation - place, year, title  [other exams]

accepted.s: Who officiated at Shivaji's coronation with Vedic rites?
o: Gaga Bhatt of Banaras or Varanasi
accepted.x: Gaga Bhatt, a learned Brahmin from Banaras or Varanasi, officiated at the coronation with Vedic rites.
accepted.tq: Test the person-place association rather than the event date.
accepted.sec: ■ Coronation - place, year, title  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following titles was adopted by Shivaji at his coronation?
accepted.x: Shivaji adopted the title “Shri Raja Shiva Chhatrapati” at his coronation.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact official title and reject familiar but unsupported royal titles.
accepted.sec: ■ Coronation - place, year, title  [other exams]

accepted.s: Shivaji was also styled as which of the following?
accepted.x: Shivaji was also styled Haindava Dharmoddharak.
accepted.tq: Test the exact title among similar-sounding religious and royal designations.
accepted.sec: ■ Coronation - place, year, title  [other exams]

accepted.s: The era started by Shivaji to assert sovereignty against the Mughals and the Sultanates was known as the
accepted.x: Shivaji began the Rajabhisheka Shaka after his coronation to assert sovereign status.
accepted.tq: Match the political purpose with the precise name of the era.
accepted.sec: ■ Coronation - place, year, title  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following rulers in chronological order of their succession in the Maratha polity:
A. Shahu
B. Sambhaji
C. Tarabai
D. Rajaram
accepted.x: The sequence was Sambhaji, Rajaram, Tarabai as regent for Shivaji II, and Shahu.
accepted.tq: Fix the first and last rulers, then place Rajaram and Tarabai between them.
accepted.sec: ■ Successors - administrative steps of each  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Sambhaji's role in the Maratha struggle?
o: He created the post of Pratinidhi after moving to Gingee.
He continued resistance, but was captured and executed by Aurangzeb in 1689.
He moved the capital to Satara and appointed Balaji Vishwanath.
He was released by Bahadur Shah I in 1707.
accepted.x: Sambhaji continued resistance against the Mughals and was captured and executed by Aurangzeb in 1689.
accepted.tq: Use the ruler-deed trap by distinguishing Sambhaji's actions from those of Rajaram and Shahu.
accepted.sec: ■ Successors - administrative steps of each  [other exams]

accepted.s: The execution of Sambhaji in 1689 had which important consequence?
o: It resulted in the Treaty of Warna.
It turned the conflict into a people's war.
It led immediately to the appointment of Balaji Vishwanath.
accepted.x: Sambhaji's execution transformed the conflict into a people's war.
accepted.tq: Connect the event with its stated political consequence instead of merely recalling the date.
accepted.sec: ■ Successors - administrative steps of each  [other exams]

accepted.s: Rajaram's movement to Gingee (Jinji) was significant because it
o: established Kolhapur as the permanent capital
secured the release of Shahu by Bahadur Shah I
drew Aurangzeb towards southern India and enabled continued resistance
accepted.x: Rajaram moved to Gingee and thereby drew Aurangzeb south while resistance continued.
accepted.tq: Test the cause-effect link between a strategic relocation and Mughal movements.
accepted.sec: ■ Successors - administrative steps of each  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which administrative post was created by Rajaram?
accepted.x: Rajaram created the post of Pratinidhi.
accepted.tq: Distinguish Rajaram's administrative innovation from military and revenue offices.
accepted.sec: ■ Successors - administrative steps of each  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Tarabai:
1. She acted as regent for her young son after Rajaram's death.
2. She led massive raids into Mughal territory.
3. Her line was later settled at Kolhapur under the Treaty of Warna.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Tarabai governed as regent, raided Mughal territory, and her line was later settled at Kolhapur under the Treaty of Warna.
accepted.tq: Check all three connected facts about a ruler before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: ■ Successors - administrative steps of each  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Treaty of Warna, associated with the settlement of Tarabai's line at Kolhapur, was concluded in
accepted.x: The Treaty of Warna was concluded in 1731 and settled Tarabai's line at Kolhapur.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the settlement year from the dates of Khed and Balaji Vishwanath's appointment.
accepted.sec: ■ Successors - administrative steps of each  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding Shahu is correct?
o: He was released by Bahadur Shah I, defeated Tarabai's forces at Khed, and ruled from Satara.
He moved to Gingee and created the post of Pratinidhi.
He was captured and executed by Aurangzeb in 1689.
He led the Marathas at Aurangzeb's death as Rajaram's widow.
accepted.x: Shahu was released by Bahadur Shah I in 1707, defeated Tarabai at Khed, and ruled from Satara.
accepted.tq: Use the ruler-deed association and reject actions belonging to Rajaram, Sambhaji or Tarabai.
accepted.sec: ■ Successors - administrative steps of each  [other exams]

accepted.s: Who was appointed Peshwa by Shahu in 1713?
accepted.x: Shahu appointed Balaji Vishwanath as Peshwa in 1713.
accepted.tq: Match the appointment with the correct ruler and year.
accepted.sec: ■ Successors - administrative steps of each  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding Aurangzeb and the Marathas?
o: Aurangzeb concluded the Treaty of Warna in 1707.
Aurangzeb died in the Deccan in 1707 without subduing the Marathas.
Aurangzeb died at Raigad in 1689 after subduing the Marathas.
Aurangzeb appointed Shahu as Peshwa in 1713.
accepted.x: Aurangzeb died in the Deccan in 1707, having failed to subdue the Marathas.
accepted.tq: Avoid the absolute-completion trap by distinguishing death in the Deccan from successful conquest.
accepted.sec: ■ Successors - administrative steps of each  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about Shivaji's revenue administration is NOT correct?
o: The state dealt directly with the cultivator in a ryotwari-type settlement.
Officials were generally paid in cash rather than through jagirs.
Peasant property was routinely seized whenever revenue could not be paid.
Hereditary deshmukhs and deshpandes were bypassed or regulated.
accepted.x: Peasant property was not seized as a normal revenue measure. Shivaji preferred cash payment of officials and direct settlement with cultivators.
accepted.tq: Find the one statement that reverses the stated protection given to peasant property.
accepted.sec: ■ Revenue and administrative terms  [other exams]

accepted.s: Under Shivaji, jagirs were abolished primarily because
o: the state abandoned land revenue collection
officials were to be paid in cash and their loyalty kept directly attached to the state
all land was transferred to hereditary deshmukhs
service land grants were made compulsory for every soldier
accepted.x: Shivaji paid officials in cash instead of granting jagirs, thereby maintaining direct loyalty to the state.
accepted.tq: Link an administrative arrangement with its stated purpose rather than treating abolition as a mere definition.
accepted.sec: ■ Revenue and administrative terms  [other exams]

accepted.s: Saranjam grants, which had been discontinued under Shivaji, were restored under
o: Bahadur Shah I and Shahu jointly
accepted.x: Saranjam, or service land grants, came back under Shahu and the Peshwas.
accepted.tq: Distinguish Shivaji's cash-payment system from the later revival of service land grants.
accepted.sec: ■ Revenue and administrative terms  [other exams]

accepted.s: Land revenue under Shivaji was assessed mainly on the basis of
o: the number of forts held by a village
the area cultivated and the crop, with the demand taken as a share of produce
the fixed cash value of every holding irrespective of cultivation
the caste of the cultivator and the distance from the capital
accepted.x: Assessment considered the cultivated area and the crop, and revenue was collected as a share of the produce.
accepted.tq: Separate the basis of assessment from later numerical rates and unrelated administrative features.
accepted.sec: ■ Revenue and administrative terms  [other exams]

accepted.s: What was the approximate change in the state share of gross produce after Annaji Datto's survey?
accepted.x: The state share was initially about 33 percent, or one-third, and later rose to 40 percent, or two-fifths, after Annaji Datto's survey.
accepted.tq: Convert the percentages into fractions and compare the before-and-after rates.
accepted.sec: ■ Revenue and administrative terms  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following was a feature of Shivaji's revenue policy?
o: Illegal cesses were abolished, famine remissions were permitted, and peasant property was not seized.
Illegal cesses were increased and famine remissions were prohibited.
Revenue was collected only through hereditary intermediaries.
Cultivators were denied any direct relationship with the state.
accepted.x: Shivaji's system included remission during famine, abolition of illegal cesses and protection against seizure of peasant property.
accepted.tq: Select the comprehensive option containing the stated welfare and revenue safeguards.
accepted.sec: ■ Revenue and administrative terms  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which pair of Maratha coins is correctly matched with its metal?
accepted.x: The Shivrai hon was a gold coin, while the Shivrai was a copper coin.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure metal association and reject the reversed pair.
accepted.sec: ■ Revenue and administrative terms  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Modi script was chiefly used for
accepted.x: Modi was the cursive script used in Marathi administrative records.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the administrative script from scripts and languages associated with other courts.
accepted.sec: ■ Revenue and administrative terms  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Rajvyavahar Kosh was associated with the replacement of
o: Persian official terms by Sanskrit terms
accepted.x: The Rajvyavahar Kosh replaced Persian official terminology with Sanskrit terminology.
accepted.tq: Test the direction of replacement in a language-policy reform.
accepted.sec: ■ Revenue and administrative terms  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following combinations is correctly matched?
1. Kathi — measuring rod
2. Jirayat — dry land
3. Bagayat — irrigated land
4. Rajvyavahar Kosh — naval manual
Select the correct answer.
accepted.x: Kathi was a measuring rod, Jirayat denoted dry land and Bagayat denoted irrigated land. The Rajvyavahar Kosh concerned official terminology, not naval matters.
accepted.tq: Find the single mismatched association and select the code containing the three correct terms.
accepted.sec: ■ Revenue and administrative terms  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following groups contains only forts classified as Giri Durg?
accepted.x: Raigad, Pratapgad, Torna and Sinhagad are hill forts, or Giri Durg. Vishalgad is a land fort, while the others in the distractors include sea forts.
accepted.tq: Classify each example by fort type and eliminate groups containing a land or sea fort.
accepted.sec: ■ Military organisation - forts, navy, hill troops

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Vishalgad is an example of Bhu Durg, or land fort. Rajgad and Panhala are hill forts.
accepted.tq: Use the fort-type classification to identify the only correctly paired example.
accepted.sec: ■ Military organisation - forts, navy, hill troops

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a sea fort listed among Shivaji's forts?
accepted.x: Sinhagad is a hill fort. Sindhudurg, Vijaydurg and Khanderi are sea forts, or Jal Durg.
accepted.tq: Find the odd location-category pair among the listed fort examples.
accepted.sec: ■ Military organisation - forts, navy, hill troops

accepted.s: Each fort under Shivaji was placed under the charge of three officers of equal rank. Which set correctly identifies them?
accepted.x: The three officers were the Havaldar, Sabnis and Sarnobat. The Sabnis handled records, while the Havaldar and Sarnobat had garrison and military responsibilities.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the fort command structure from the Ashtapradhan and army categories.
accepted.sec: ■ Military organisation - forts, navy, hill troops

accepted.s: In the organisation of a Maratha fort, the Sabnis was primarily associated with
o: collection of chauth from the Mughals
accepted.x: The Sabnis was the officer responsible for records in the fort administration.
accepted.tq: Match the office with its specific function rather than its general military setting.
accepted.sec: ■ Military organisation - forts, navy, hill troops

accepted.s: The infantry recruited from the hill regions in Shivaji's army was known as
accepted.x: The hill troops in Shivaji's army were known as Mavali infantry.
accepted.tq: Separate the hill infantry designation from the two cavalry categories.
accepted.sec: ■ Military organisation - forts, navy, hill troops

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Maratha cavalry:
1. Bargirs were provided horses and equipment by the state.
2. Shiledars maintained their own horses.
3. Both terms referred to categories of cavalry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Bargirs were state-equipped cavalrymen, whereas Shiledars supplied their own horses; both were cavalry categories.
accepted.tq: Compare the two confusable cavalry categories before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: ■ Military organisation - forts, navy, hill troops

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the responsibility described?
1. Havaldar — garrison commander
2. Sabnis — records
3. Sarnobat — military officer
Select the correct answer.
accepted.x: The Havaldar commanded the garrison, the Sabnis maintained records and the Sarnobat was the military officer. All three associations are correct.
accepted.tq: Verify each office-function pair independently before choosing the full set.
accepted.sec: ■ Military organisation - forts, navy, hill troops

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about Shivaji's naval policy is correct?
o: He built a navy and established sea forts such as Sindhudurg and Kolaba.
He abolished naval establishments and relied exclusively on Mughal ships.
He used sea forts solely as revenue offices.
He built only hill forts and avoided the Konkan coast.
accepted.x: Shivaji built a navy and developed sea forts including Sindhudurg and Kolaba.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the positive naval-building policy from absolute statements about exclusive reliance on land forces.
accepted.sec: ■ Military organisation - forts, navy, hill troops

accepted.s: The naval bases at Sindhudurg and Vijaydurg were important because they guarded the
accepted.x: Sindhudurg and Vijaydurg served as naval bases guarding the Konkan coast.
accepted.tq: Connect named naval bases with their geographical strategic zone.
accepted.sec: ■ Military organisation - forts, navy, hill troops

accepted.s: Shivaji is regarded in the cited contemporary reference as the
o: Father of the Indian Air Force
Father of the Indian Coast Guard
accepted.x: Shivaji is regarded as the Father of the Indian Navy in the cited February 2026 reference.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact honorific while rejecting nearby modern military designations.
accepted.sec: ■ Military organisation - forts, navy, hill troops

accepted.s: According to the Adnyapatra of Ramachandrapant Amatya, forts were regarded as
accepted.x: The Adnyapatra states that forts were the core of the state.
accepted.tq: Recall the distinctive maxim and distinguish it from the administrative functions of forts.
accepted.sec: ■ Military organisation - forts, navy, hill troops

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Shivaji's military organisation is NOT correct?
o: The Battle of Salher in 1672 saw the Mughals defeated in open battle.
Jagirs were the regular means of paying the standing army and securing its loyalty.
The standing army was organised without jagir-based payment.
He maintained a standing army paid in cash.
accepted.x: Shivaji's standing army was paid in cash rather than jagirs so that loyalty remained directly attached to the state. The Marathas defeated the Mughals in open battle at Salher in 1672.
accepted.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the cash-payment principle and use the related battle fact as confirmation.
